transcript: Last night I saw New York, New York on Broadway, a new musical that follows various characters all trying to make their dreams come true in New York in the 19 forties, shortly after the war. The main characters are Jimmy and Francine, who are both musicians with big dreams who meet one another and fall in love, a typical love story. One of the highlights of the production is the design. The set design in particular is remarkable. The performances are really good too, but I thought the storytelling was generally a little flimsy, with there not being a lot of opportunity for us to really understand the backgrounds of the characters, and this makes it kind of hard to understand the character's motivations throughout the piece. There are also a lot of different supporting characters in addition to the 2 leads, and you never really get a deep look at any of them enough to be that invested. The show is still in preview, so they have some time to sharpen this up, hopefully. Regardless, New York, New York is big and flashy in the way you want it to be. The music is decent, and there are some really gorgeously staged sequences, so I was definitely entertained with that. Another playbill for my collection.
